Key Research Thinking Patterns: Genomic-Phenotypic Mapping via High-Throughput Mutagenesis: Utilizing Random Barcode Transposon Site Sequencing (RB-TnSeq) and pooled mutant fitness assays to systematically identify gene essentiality and metabolic capabilities in model organisms like Desulfovibrio vulgaris, linking genotype to physiological traits such as bioremediation potential.

Molecular Surveillance and Variant Tracking: Deploying allele-specific RT-qPCR, digital PCR, and bioinformatics pipelines (C-WAP, Freyja) on wastewater samples to detect and quantify specific viral mutations (e.g., SARS-CoV-2 Delta to Omicron transitions), providing real-time epidemiological early warning signals.

Assay Validation and Confounder Resolution: Rigorously validating environmental molecular assays by distinguishing true fecal indicators from non-fecal false positives using statistical modeling (Generalized Linear Models) and comparative techniques (Enterolert, Biolog profiling) to ensure data reliability in complex environmental matrices.

Translational Standardization of Bacterial WBE: Adapting viral-centric wastewater surveillance frameworks to bacterial targets by addressing technical bottlenecks such as bacterial partitioning, plasmid copy number estimation, and viable but non-culturable (VBNC) states to establish standardized protocols for monitoring pathogens like S. Typhi and antimicrobial resistance genes.
Summary Description: Kara B. De León bridges microbial physiology and advanced public health surveillance, specializing in Wastewater-Based Epidemiology (WBE). Her research integrates high-throughput genomic tools, such as RB-TnSeq, to elucidate microbial metabolism and bioremediation potential in environmental isolates. Transitioning to epidemiology, she pioneers real-time monitoring of SARS-CoV-2 variants and bacterial pathogens in wastewater, employing allele-specific RT-qPCR and specialized bioinformatics pipelines to correlate viral signals with demographic factors. A key focus is validating water quality assays to resolve environmental confounders and establishing standardized protocols for bacterial WBE, addressing challenges like VBNC states and plasmid dynamics. Her work significantly advances the translation of molecular data into actionable public health insights and environmental management strategies.
